Abstract
We construct a source–readout realization of the Wilson Yang–Mills construction within
Jeremy Rodgers’s Shadow Theory. The framework separates an admitted native support, its
literal preparation, the realized physical histories and the readouts that recover configurations,
effective quantities, field labels and operator correlations. Reflective mathematics makes the re-
lation between these layers explicit: reverse sections establish coverage, fibres identify redundant
or discarded information, operation identities establish compatibility, and residuals quantify de-
partures from exact recovery.
The paper proves normalized finite-measure recovery and classifies the frame fibres; trans-
ports activity domains and budgets; recovers the stationary vertical discrepancy from its residual;
and establishes the compatibility of coefficient readers, physical equation quotients, Hilbert-
space reconstruction, phases and operator products. These interfaces are developed through
the complete quadratic, nonlinear, marked-integration, calibration, continuum and stress calcu-
lations. One compatible Wilson family carries full fixed-period mesh limits followed by the per-
mitted refined volume limit. Its selected centered trace has the asymptotic r8 log2(1/r)GΘ(r) →
3 dimR g/π4, with the stated finite mass-shell and Maxwell comparison exclusions. No positive
mass gap is asserted.
OpenAI’s underlying Lean construction is presented through the supplied expanded mathe-
matical translation. The contribution here is the explicit source–readout construction and its
recovery proofs, with all substantive Yang–Mills derivations retained. The given gauge group,
faithful representation, four-dimensional Wilson law and analytic hypotheses remain the physical
inputs to this conditional realization.
Authorship. Jeremy Rodgers originated Shadow Theory, the source–readout architecture and the Source
Lift protocol, and directed this research using those methods and examples. AI assisted in carrying out the
work.
Release. This paper and its standalone mathematical companion form one Zenodo release under the DOI
above.
Funding. No external funding.

Introduction
The Wilson Yang–Mills construction joins several kinds of mathematics: finite group-valued config-
urations and probability measures, effective actions and stationary variables, local coefficient spaces
and equation quotients, continuum correlations, Hilbert-space fields and spectral readers. Recover-
ing its conclusion requires these objects and operations to belong to one compatible construction.
Equality of final formulas alone does not establish that differentiation, integration, calibration,
quotienting and limiting operations preserve the information needed by the next stage.
This paper addresses that problem using Shadow Theory’s source–readout architecture and
Source Lift protocol, originated by Jeremy Rodgers [3]. Rodgers directed the research through
that framework and its worked examples; AI assisted its execution.
A Source Lift constructs
an admitted native support, its literal preparation and a realized sector containing the physical
histories and auxiliary data. Typed readouts then recover the objects of the target derivation. Their
sections establish reverse coverage, their fibres identify the distinctions removed, and their operation
identities establish how the derivation passes through the realization. Reflective mathematics is the
explicit accounting for these maps, domains, residuals and recovery claims. Section 2 introduces
this framework before applying it.
The application is OpenAI’s underlying Lean Yang–Mills construction, available here through its
supplied expanded mathematical translation [2]. The companion paper, A Wilson Yang–Mills Con-
struction: A Natural-Language Mathematical Exposition, presents that construction on its own [1].
Both papers are included in the same Zenodo release, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24173681, and each
contains its essential mathematics. The companion emphasizes the construction itself. This paper
develops the source–readout realization, the reflective analysis of its interfaces and the recovery
proofs throughout the same derivation.
Mathematical contribution.
The finite realization has an explicit section, a complete frame-
fibre description and an exactly normalized measure pushforward. The family of histories is sup-
ported by an admitted fan, with a groupoid equivalence on each finite realized leaf. The reconstruc-
tion then proves frame-blindness of flags and budgets, ordered-derivative and activity-norm recovery,
and quantitative recovery of an eliminated vertical discrepancy from the stationary residual. At the
field stage it gives the curl/radial section and its gauge fibre, the calibrated coefficient reader, and
the physical quotient defined by all spectator readings, with inclusions and derivatives descending
to that quotient. The Hilbert-space, phase, product and collision-extension interfaces retain their
actual domains and choices. These results explain precisely which operations are recovered, rather
than treating every reduction as the same kind of inverse.
The full Yang–Mills calculations remain in the paper. They use Wilson’s lattice formulation [5],
reflection positivity and reconstruction [11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16], renormalization and cluster meth-
ods [17, 18, 19], and the conventional one-loop coefficient [20, 21]. The given physical inputs and
the exact public conclusion are stated in Section 4; the assumption and dependency registers collect
their scope. The earlier Einstein source–readout reconstruction [4] provides a model of exposition:
define the primitives and maps, derive the operation, prove coverage, and identify the residual or
information loss. Its gravitational results are not Yang–Mills premises.
Organization and reading conventions.
The framework, public conclusion and analytic con-
ventions fix the objects, target and normalizations. Native admission, the finite realization and
the interface table then introduce the common witness. The construction follows dependency or-
der: quadratic kernels; nonlinear geometry and budgets; marked integration and reset; stationary
graphs, calibrated histories and convergence; labels, shell charges and physical detection; the full

Source–readout and reflective mathematics: the objects and the
task
The framework distinguishes the mathematical input from its native antecedent.
The supplied
mathematical source is the expanded translation of OpenAI’s underlying Lean Yang–Mills construc-
tion. The native source support is an admitted object in Rodgers’s source–readout architecture: it
carries a dependency order and marked finite supports. The physical lattice, group, fields and law
enter in the realization over that support. This separation lets the paper construct and compare
the actual readout operations while retaining the provenance of their physical assumptions.
In ordinary terms, a readout is a specified way of obtaining a mathematical object from a richer
record. A lattice configuration can be read from links written in independently chosen endpoint
frames. An effective action can be read from a function of retained and auxiliary variables by
evaluating on its stationary graph. A physical field label can be read from a coefficient vector after
identifying vectors that every allowed spectator test fails to distinguish. These are different maps,
with different fibres. The paper proves their recovery statements on their respective domains; it
does not treat them as interchangeable instances of an unrestricted inverse.
The term reflective mathematics means mathematics of the readout objects together with ex-
plicit accounting for their source–readout relations. In Rodgers’s Source Lift protocol this includes
the maps and domains, admission conditions, distinctions removed by a map, residuals, available
reconstruction routes and the status of each claim. Here those items are made concrete by the
following definitions and calculations. Reflection is this source-aware accounting within the math-
ematics. It is not an additional dynamical law, and it does not assert that a theory selects its own
physical inputs [3].
This use of reflective is distinct from reflection positivity, the positive-pairing property of Eu-
clidean correlations used later to construct a Hilbert space.
Reflection positivity is one of the
specific mathematical operations accounted for here; it is not the definition of reflective mathe-
matics. Likewise, matching status profiles does not establish an equivalence: an equivalence must
preserve the specified objects and operations through actual maps.

2.4
What is retained, what is removed, and what is selected
The reflective record distinguishes several mathematically different situations. A redescription fibre
consists of presentations of the same retained object, as in the frame example. An observational
quotient identifies records indistinguishable by a specified family of readers. A stationary restric-
tion selects a solution of an auxiliary equation. A controlled comparison retains a nonzero error.
A selection retains a complement, calibration, phase or extraction witness that the argument is
permitted to choose. None is automatically the same as another.

The contribution of the reflective organization can now be stated precisely. It identifies which
mathematical object a formula reads, whether a reverse section covers the next step, which operation
descends, and which discrepancy or choice must survive a reduction. Its claims are proved by the
actual maps and estimates, not by assigning a status word. The gauge group, dimension, Wilson
action, physical normalization and analytic assumptions remain the supplied realization inputs
except for the particular dependencies derived within the construction. Alternative realizations
can be placed over the same native support; its admission therefore does not select those inputs.
The remaining sections implement this framework through the entire supplied derivation.

Provenance and mathematical contract
3.1
Source provenance and attribution
OpenAI is credited for the underlying Lean Yang–Mills construction. The mathematical source used
here is the project’s expanded natural-language extraction, prepared with AI assistance: Wilson
Yang–Mills Construction: Mathematical Translation [2]. Its complete text is reproduced unchanged
in this release as sources/Full_pre_source_translation.md. The 15,788-line source is numbered
using universal-newline counting; the package manifest records its full hash. No model, repository,
version or generation-date identifier is assigned where the supplied materials do not establish one.
Jeremy Rodgers originated Shadow Theory, the source–readout architecture and the Source
Lift protocol, and directed this research using those methods and examples.
He is the author
of the reconstruction and its mathematical presentation. AI assisted in developing and checking
the realization, preparing the exposition and performing the recorded computational checks. The
source–readout definitions and proofs needed for this application are contained in this paper.
3.2
Mathematical contract
The physical group and faithful representation, lattice dimension, Wilson law, preparation and
analytic conditions are the inputs to the realized sector. The public conclusion is recovered with its
original hypotheses, witnesses and order of limits: the full mesh limit at each suitable fixed period
precedes the permitted refined volume limit. Native admission and physical realization remain
distinct layers, as developed in Section 2.1.
The derivations are retained with their original equation tags. The explicit formula amendments,
typography clarifications and local recovery corrections are documented with their supporting cal-
culations in Section I.1.
The preserved source remains unchanged.
The verification record in
Section J distinguishes general recovery proofs, finite computational checks and the scope of the
supplied Yang–Mills construction.

8
The source support of the realized family, its lift groupoid and
its interfaces
The preceding two sections give the lift of one finite lattice: an admitted antecedent (Proposi-
tion 6.1), a redundant realization, its readout and its section (Theorems 7.1 and 7.2). The supplied
construction, however, is not one lattice. It is a countable family of finite histories, indexed by
a cutoff, a period and a scale level, together with comparisons between them, auxiliary reference
volumes, coefficient spaces of field labels, an imported free comparison theory and several successive
limits. This section develops the source-side structure that is needed to carry that family, and states
what that structure does and does not determine. It has four parts: the admitted support; the lift
groupoid of a single leaf; the sectors and interfaces of the supplied construction, with the status of
each discrepancy; and the separation of what follows from the source side from what is supplied as
realization data. Nothing in this section is used as a hypothesis by the supplied derivations that
follow; it is the frame in which their source–readout formulations are stated.
8.1
A fan of marked dependencies
Let I be a nonempty countable set. The fan ΦI has vertices {r}∪{la : a ∈I}, dependency preorder
generated by r ≺la for every a, and one marked token ma for each a ∈I, with support {r, la}. The
lineage, invariant and intrinsic boundary data of ma are those of the walking marked dependency

X⋆, transported along the map ca : X⋆→ΦI, ca(0) = r, ca(1) = la. For a subset F ⊆I write ΦF

Proposition 8.1 (Admission of the fan). For every countable I the fan ΦI is admitted. More
precisely:
1. for finite F, ΦF is obtained from |F| copies of X⋆by successive attachments along the root
face {0}, and is admitted;
2. for F ⊆F ′ the inclusion ΦF →ΦF ′ is a strong map, and ΦI is the directed colimit of the ΦF
over finite F ⊆I; this colimit is stabilizing;
3. distinct leaves are incomparable: for a ̸= b neither la ⪯lb nor lb ⪯la.
Proof. The admission construction of [3] is the least isomorphism-saturated class containing the
initial witnesses, among them X⋆, and closed under the specified finite attachments along source
faces, presentation-preserving retracts and stabilizing directed colimits. The root {0} of X⋆is a
source face: it is predecessor-closed, and it is lineage- and boundary-closed because the marked
token is not supported in it and the intrinsic boundary is empty. (1) Attaching a further copy of
X⋆to ΦF along the identification of its root with r is a pushout along that face. The attaching
map is strong and reflects marks, since no marked support lies in the face. The pushout adds one
vertex, one strict pair and one marked token, and leaves every existing support, strict pair and
lineage datum unchanged; the candidate conditions (finite nonempty supports each containing a
strict pair, well-typed inherited data) therefore hold in ΦF∪{a}. Induction on |F| gives admission.
(2) An inclusion of subfans preserves the preorder, the marking, the supports with their strict pairs
and the inherited data, and is injective; it is therefore strong. Every finite set of vertices and tokens
of ΦI lies in some ΦF with F finite, and its preorder, supports and inherited data are the same in
every larger subfan; this is the stabilization condition. (3) The preorder is generated by the pairs
r ≺la, and neither a pushout along the root nor the colimit adds a relation between leaves.
This is the same admission that supports the family of prepared paths in the gravitational
reconstruction [4]; only the index set and the realized sector differ. The literal preparation of a leaf
is
Ya = Jreal(ΦI, ma) ∼= Y⋆,
the preparation of Proposition 6.1, by restriction along ca.

leaves, with ma 7→mσ(a); thus Aut(ΦI) ∼= Sym(I).
2. The fold map φ : ΦI →X⋆, φ(r) = 0, φ(la) = 1, φ(ma) = m⋆, is strong, and φca = id for
every a.

strictly below at least two others, and permutes the remaining vertices. It preserves supports, so
it sends ma to the token supported on {r, lσ(a)}. Conversely each permutation of I defines such
a map, and it preserves the inherited data because these are transported from the same X⋆along
the maps ca. (2) φ preserves the preorder and the strict pairs r ≺la 7→0 ≺1, carries each support
bijectively onto {0, 1}, so is injective on marked supports, and preserves the inherited data by their
definition. (3) is Proposition 8.1(2).

8.3
Sectors, interfaces and discrepancies of the supplied construction
A realized family over the fan consists of: an injective labelling λ of the leaves by the index set of
the construction; for each leaf a a raw datum za in a sector over Ya, with its discrepancy column;
and, for each interface e between sectors s and t, maps Le, Re into a common comparison space
and the retained discrepancy
δe = de(Lezs, Rezt).
An interface is exact if δe = 0 identically, controlled if δe is bounded in a declared norm on a declared
regime, and selected if it involves a choice (of a subsequence, a complement or a representative)
that is retained as a witness. The index set of the supplied construction consists of the triples
(N, p, i) with cutoffindex N, period index p and scale level 0 ≤i ≤N, together with labels for the
reference tori of the beacons and for the free comparison theory. The numbers attached to a label
(lattice side, block length, clock value, stage) are read from the one calendar c of Theorem 14.16.
The sectors are the following.
(S1) Finite Wilson history at (N, p): z = (r, A) ∈ZN,p with the law eμ; readout π.

layout and the evaluated density.
(S3) Stationary corridor of a blocking step: pairs (x, v) of retained and vertical coordinates with
the residual S(x, v) (Section 14).
(S4) Reference views: the folded reference tori of the beacons and of the reference chart.

of the realized record, with the full limit in the cutofftaken at each fixed period before the limit
in the period along the refined sequence. Second, the rows fall into the method’s exactness classes
without exception being made for convenience: I1–I3, I5 and I12 are exact; I4 and I6 are on-shell

established by congruence statements; I7, I8, I13, I14 and I16 are controlled approximations with

8.4
What follows from the source side and what is supplied
The division is the following, and it is used without further comment in the formulations below.
From the source side. The admitted fan provides a support with countably many marked cells
(Proposition 8.1); no relation between distinct cells and no preferred labelling (Proposition 8.2);
and the reduction of every finite statement to an admitted finite support. On each leaf the realized
branch has contractible lift groupoids (Theorem 8.3). These are structural facts. They contain no
dynamics.
Supplied as realization data. Everything that makes the family a Yang–Mills construction is
chosen in the realized sector: the compact group G ⊆U(m) with simple nonabelian Lie algebra;
the four-dimensional periodic lattices and the Wilson action; the blocking maps and the stationary
corridors; the calendar c; the calibration value  ̄β and the blocking penalty one; the label algebra
and the free comparison theory; and every estimate. The labelling of leaves by (N, p, i), and hence
the notions of finer, larger and coarser, are of this kind.
Derived within the realization. Some quantities are neither chosen nor source-side: they are
computed from the realization data by the supplied construction. The slope s = 11CA/(24π2) is the
coefficient of the logarithm in the explicit annular integral (DR5); the amplitude AG = 3 dimR g/π4
is a Wick contraction (Theorem 24.1); the one-dimensionality of the translation Ward kernel of
the free comparison theory (FS10) and the O(4) covariance of the hierarchy (Theorem 19.3) are
consequences.
Not obtained. No selection theorem is proved, and none is claimed. The method’s test for a
source-derived premise is to look for inequivalent raw realizations over the same admitted support
and the same literal preparations. Here they exist in abundance: replacing the group, the dimension
of the lattice, or the Wilson action by another gauge-invariant local action gives a different realized
sector over the same fan ΦI, with the same lift-groupoid theorem. Admission therefore does not
select the gauge group, the dimension, the action or the coupling history. The recovery proved in
this paper is conditional in exactly this sense: given the supplied construction as realization data,
its objects, operations, limits and conclusions are recovered through the readouts, with the stated
exactness classes. This distinguishes an explicit mathematical recovery theorem from selection of
the physical realization.

A letter is of one of four disjoint types: a block packet A, an old forced index q, a regular

footprints of all its letters. In particular it contains every seed and every forced read. Admission
requires all of the following: the overlap graph of letter footprints is connected, the packet letters

16
Radial jets, calibrated labels and the free Maxwell comparison
hierarchy
From local coefficients to usable field labels.
The first objects are finite Taylor coefficient
spaces. Curl reads their linearized curvature, and radial reconstruction provides an explicit section
on closed homogeneous two-forms.
The Maxwell equation imposes a further condition on that
curvature. Polynomial labels are then sampled by finite local cylinders, with calibrated coefficient
maps and a free comparison hierarchy. Keeping polynomial position degree, engineering weight and
field count distinct is necessary for the later detector and scaling arguments. The free hierarchy is
a supplied comparison sector; its presence does not assert that the interacting hierarchy is free.
Before the detector on physical coefficient space can be constructed, the supplied construction
builds the label algebra, its local lattice representatives, the calibrated coefficient changes and the
complete free comparison hierarchy with its shell charges. This section gives that construction in
full, from the radial Taylor variables to the elimination of higher-degree vector and angular defects;
each subsection is followed by its source–readout formulation. The labels are the first place where
the recovery problem is posed for fields and not only for measures: a label is a source record, its
lattice cylinder is a realization, and its Taylor readings are the readout.
16.1

order j ≥0, a radial potential coefficient is a family Ai of symmetric (j + 1)-linear maps from

Source–readout formulation.
The free hierarchy is an imported comparison realization: a sec-
ond realized sector over the same label algebra, built from the explicit kernel (FM2). It is not the
interacting theory and nothing in its construction refers to the Wilson history. Its role in the sup-
plied construction is that of a calibrated yardstick: detection, charge and Ward-kernel statements
proved for it are transferred to the interacting hierarchy only through the comparison estimates
that follow. The label algebra, with its restriction map, is the interface between the two sectors in
the sense of the method: both hierarchies are read on the same labels, and discrepancies between
them are retained as interface residuals.
The realized sector of the free hierarchy is explicit: its source record is the kernel K of (FM2)
on the fixed real symbol space, its readout is the family of moments Mn of (FM3), and the only
operations are multilinear extension, differentiation in the insertion points and restriction to smaller
label sets. Each of these commutes with the moment formula because the sum over matchings is
finite and the kernel is real analytic away from coincident points. No statement about the interacting
measure is contained in this subsection.

Surjectivity of the reflection attachment
The boundary attachment J is an isometry from a complete Hilbert space, so its range is closed. For
regularized words integrated against Fourier transforms of compact smooth tests, the boundary tilt
identifies the vector with an attached boundary distribution on the chilled test. Explicitly the joint
pairing gives ⟨A, A⟩= ⟨B, B⟩; regularized approximants to B and partial-boundary convergence
give ⟨A, B⟩= ⟨B, B⟩. Thus ∥A−B∥2 = 0. The strict-time and independently heated constructions
below supply these pairing and tilt inputs. Compact cutoffs approximate Fourier Schwartz tests.
The word bound C∥f∥L1 and closed range extend membership to all integrated regularized words.
Pairing a pointwise word with a vector orthogonal to the range gives zero smeared pairings; con-
tinuity makes the pairing zero everywhere. Double orthogonal complement and closedness place
pointwise words in the range. Strictly ordered positive-time Euclidean words are regularized words:
choose regularization below the first time and all gaps, then recursively apply local fields, trans-
lations and heat operators. This reproduces the reflection plant with its insertion representatives;
quotient representatives agree against every future word and give the same plant. For arbitrary
future words sort times by permutation symmetry, then add εi to the ith time. For small posi-
tive epsilon the configurations remain separated with strict positive time order and converge back.
Expanding plant squared-distance into three table pairings proves norm continuity from smooth
separated correlations. Since the range is closed, the unperturbed plant also lies in it. Future
plants span densely by GNS, so J is onto. Here GNS denotes the Gelfand–Naimark–Segal positive-
functional construction [8, 9]; the domain and quotient recovery are the ones specified above. The
lift retains boundary word tests, chilled tests, representatives and heat/translation recursion. Re-
covery preserves the pairing identities and plant norm limits, transporting this surjectivity to the
lifted completed space with its actual word domain.

The order of choices in the spectral sign walk
We record the quantitative induction that supplies the small mixed-band bound in (RT6). Let Q
be the finite set of axes being tested, with two signs assigned so that each axis has an opposite-sign
partner. Let U ⊆Q be the axes whose width exponent is still allowed to be negative, and let i be
the active axis. A finite route alternates signs and removes the currently visited axis from U. Such
a route exists by induction on |U|: if the active axis is in U, remove it and move to an opposite
partner. If it is not, choose an axis still in U; reach it directly if its sign is opposite, and otherwise
take one opposite-sign detour. This reduces the nonempty set after at most two such moves.
The induction statement is uniform in a width vector w with −K ≤wj ≤a, wi ≤d, and wj ≥0
outside U, for every 0 ≤d ≤a. It asserts a residual budget δ > 0 after sufficiently high moment
order, for nonnegative even compact profiles and all fixed support factors. If U is empty, the direct
spectral moment bound of order zero has a finite price exponent D. Choose a > 0 with aD < δ.
The nonnegative widths then pay its residual by that budget.
At an induction step from axis i to an opposite-sign axis j, first obtain the future bandwidth

Ward kernel transfer and the rotation action
We explain how these identities extend to general tuples and to a group action. Differentiating a
shell integral is allowed because its fixed compact annulus remains separated under small move-
ments of the distinguished point. Differentiation acts both on the correlation and on the centered
angular coefficient. The latter derivative is the relevant constant translation coefficient. Hence
every position derivative of a line Ward test is again a finite sum of line Ward tests for successor-
degree labels. The all-order scaling comparison (WS7) transports these tests to the free quotient,
where the translation and angular actions are explicit derivatives of polynomials. Finitely many
separated reading maps suffice at each finite degree, by the detector argument in (WS4)–(WS5).
Their matrices converge to injective free matrices. This transfers the free rank statements for the
spaces of possible internal defects and forces any such defect to vanish. Thus the translation shell
map is one positive scalar c times the already constructed derivative, and the angular rows, divided
by c, satisfy the Ward identity at every separated tuple.
The finite-dimensional rank arguments just used have two different domains. For translation
rows, the domain at cap d is the real subspace of Q4

Conclusion
The Wilson Yang–Mills construction admits an explicit source–readout realization across its full
chain of finite, effective and continuum objects. An admitted fan supports the compatible histories.
The finite frame reader has a complete fibre description, a reverse section and an exactly normal-
ized measure pushforward. Activities and their budgets are recovered in the transported norm.
A stationary section eliminates vertical variables while its retained residual controls the off-shell
discrepancy. Calibrated histories and their running belong to one recipe and calendar, and the
continuum hierarchy retains the full inner mesh limit before the outer volume refinement.
At the field interfaces, radial reconstruction, coefficient readers and the spectator-null quotient
make explicit which local representatives are identified. Inclusions, derivatives, Hilbert completion,
character evaluation and product readers act compatibly on those retained objects. The stress and
trace calculation uses the same physical table, phase and comparison labels through the universal-
radius and spectral arguments. Its result is the precise short-distance asymptotic and the stated
comparison exclusions of the supplied construction.
The mathematical purpose of Rodgers’s framework is realized in these interfaces: it supplies a
connected account of the operations that survive projection, the reverse coverage available, and the
information, residuals and choices that a reduction must retain. The result is a complete conditional
recovery of the specified Yang–Mills derivation. Together with the standalone companion in this
release, it provides both the construction and its reflective source–readout analysis in fully editable
mathematical form.
29
Attribution of the source and mathematical background
Jeremy Rodgers originated Shadow Theory, the source–readout architecture and the Source Lift pro-
tocol, and directed this research. The framework’s role here is the explicit realization and recovery
analysis developed throughout the paper. OpenAI is credited for the underlying Lean Yang–Mills
construction, represented in this edition by the expanded mathematical translation [2]. AI assisted
in carrying out the research and preparing the manuscript. The earlier Einstein reconstruction [4] is
a methodological and expository example; the present Yang–Mills derivations are supplied locally.
Wilson’s lattice gauge formulation is credited to Wilson [5], compact-group invariant measure
to Haar [6], and the pairing formula to Wick [7]. The Euclidean reconstruction framework and
reflection positivity are credited to Osterwalder and Schrader [11, 12], with the lattice-gauge setting
of [13] and the chessboard estimates of [14]. The positive-functional construction is credited to
Gelfand, Naimark and Segal [8, 9], and the character-algebra approximation theorem to Stone [10].
Renormalization and cluster-expansion background is provided by [17, 18, 19, 15], the axiomatic
field framework by [16], and the one-loop coefficient by [20, 21]. The precise hypotheses, parameter
orders, domains and readout definitions used in this application are stated in the corresponding
derivations.

panion A Wilson Yang–Mills Construction: A Natural-Language Mathematical Exposition form
one Zenodo release under DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24173681. The release contains both editable source

Verification, limitations and reproducibility
Mathematical and computational evidence.
The general source–readout results are proved
in the text.
The verification package also includes exact-arithmetic and finite-model checks of
the formulas used by the reconstruction. The retained arithmetic suite records 28 passing checks:
angular moments and the pole coefficient; the stress stencil moments; the free Hessian and third
derivative, detector tables and conserved combination; the differentiated covariance; the Laplacian
and regularized fundamental solution; the rotation idempotents; the exponent systems and activity
rates; the beacon fourth difference; calendar plateaus; and shooting coefficients. Its script and
receipt are verification/check_lift_numbers.py and the corresponding result record.
The retained structure suite records nine passing checks. It tests frame equivariance and fibre
transitivity on the symmetric group on three letters over a triangle, the automorphism/stabilizer
and holonomy-centralizer identifications, the fibre law, fan automorphisms and the single-axis
exterior-division identity.
Its script is verification/check_lift_structure.py.
The focused
amendment suite separately checks the ordered noncommutative residual, distinct base and varied
Gaussian covariances, the two-sided shooting band, geometric radius matching, principal predictor
cancellation and the Gaussian normalization. Records distinguish retained results from executions
made for this release. Finite computations support these specific calculations; the general proofs
are the displayed arguments.
Scope.
The reconstruction takes the expanded translation of OpenAI’s underlying Lean con-
struction as its mathematical input; it does not re-execute or independently certify that formal
development. The recovered conclusions retain the supplied hypotheses and comparison classes,
and do not assert a positive mass gap. The group, dimension, Wilson action and physical prepa-
ration remain realization inputs. Native admission establishes the supporting structure, while the
specific operators, estimates and choices give the Yang–Mills realization described in the body.
Several recovery statements have essential local qualifications. On gauge-invariant quantities
the frame reader is an identity encoding; its larger role is to organize compatible non-invariant
charts and the interfaces of Table 2.
The label-reader inverse is bounded at each fixed level,

rather than uniformly in the level (Theorem 16.3). Beacon constants belong to the fixed reference
tori. Scaling maps retain their selected radius sequences (Theorem 23.2), and calibrated-history
uniqueness is within the fixed recipe (Theorem 14.29). The proof of the full trace limit uses the
stronger universal subsequence property on the same table and phase. These qualifications are
retained in the respective mathematical statements.
Reproducibility.
The shared release contains both complete editable LATEX trees, the
unchanged expanded source, source coverage and amendment records, the focused checks and the
retained arithmetic and structure suites with their receipts. Build instructions identify the
toolchain and commands, and output hashes bind the resulting files. The PDFs are compiled with
resolved references and inspected in rendered form. The source–readout definitions and essential
proofs are included in this article; no private methodological file is required to read or reproduce
its mathematical presentation.
